claims.text: Early preg: quantitative serum beta-hCG, blood type and Rh, and USU pelvic US.
claims.quote: For women with a documented pregnancy, several tests are done: Quantitative serum beta-hCG level Blood typing and Rh testing Usually pelvic ultrasound

claims.text: Heavy bleed: add CBC and type and screen or cross-match; for major hemorrhage or shock, PT/PTT, fibrinogen and fibrin split prod.
claims.quote: If bleeding is substantial, testing should also include complete blood count and either type and screen (for abnormal antibodies) or cross-matching. For major hemorrhage or shock, prothrombin time/partial thromboplastin time (PT/PTT), fibrinogen level, and fibrin split products are also determined.

claims.text: Discriminatory zone: a beta-hCG of ≥ 1000 to 2000 mIU/mL = commonly used as the level above which transvaginal US should show an intrauterine preg; use your facility's level.
claims.quote: Levels of ≥ 1000 to 2000 mIU/mL are commonly used as the discriminatory zone; however, some studies show that a gestational sac may not be visualized until the hCG is ≥ 3510 IU/L (1). The discriminatory level at the facility where the test is done should be used to guide clinical management

claims.text: Serial beta-hCG in stable, low-suspicion pts: it normally doubles every 1.4 to 2.1 days; in ectopic preg or abortion it rises more slowly.
claims.quote: If the patient is stable and clinical suspicion for ectopic pregnancy is low, serial beta-hCG levels may be done on an outpatient basis. Normally, the level doubles every 1.4 to 2.1 days up to 41 days gestation; in ectopic pregnancy (and in abortions), levels may be lower than expected by dates and usually do not double as rapidly.

claims.text: Late preg: pelvic US, CBC and type and screen, sometimes coag tests, and possibly Kleihauer-Betke.
claims.quote: The tests should include the following: Pelvic ultrasound Complete blood count (CBC) and type and screen Sometimes, coagulation tests Possibly Kleihauer-Betke testing

claims.text: Late-pregnancy US: a norm placenta and norm cord and vessel insertion exclude previa and vasa previa; abruption and uterine rupture are clin diagnoses.
claims.quote: A normal placenta and normal cord and vessel insertion exclude placenta previa and vasa previa. Although ultrasonography sometimes shows placental abruption, this test is not sufficiently reliable to distinguish placental abruption from uterine rupture. These diagnoses are made clinically

claims.text: Kleihauer-Betke measures fetal blood in the maternal circ to dose additional Rho(D) immune globulin.
claims.quote: The Kleihauer-Betke test can be done to measure the amount of fetal blood in the maternal circulation and determine the need for additional doses of Rho(D) immune globulin to prevent maternal sensitization.
